_description: Advanced node taxonomy for senior VFX artists building Unreal materials for Niagara, mesh effects, and environment-aware shaders. Use this after the foundational taxonomy when the effect needs stronger depth integration, procedural logic, platform control, or mesh-aware deformation.
overview: Senior-level VFX material work often moves beyond simple tint, panning, and mask shaping. The next layer is about making effects integrate with scene depth, object scale, world space, shader variants, packed texture data, procedural shape generation, and animated mesh data. These nodes are not always the first nodes to place, but they are often the nodes that make the effect production-ready.
use_after_foundation: Read Knowledge/Materials/Techniques/vfx_artist_essential_node_taxonomy.json first. This advanced taxonomy assumes the artist already understands Niagara data links, basic UV motion, masking, and simple deformation.

categories.display_name: Node xu ly khong gian va chieu sau
categories.why_it_matters: These nodes make the effect sit inside the world correctly instead of clipping harshly against geometry or ignoring world-space context.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Soften the edge where translucent particles intersect world geometry.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: For translucent cards that touch environment geometry, DepthFade is often mandatory. It should usually be one of the last operations on the opacity branch, not the primary shape generator.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Read or compare scene depth for view-based or depth-based effects.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Use SceneDepth or PixelDepth when the effect must react to what the camera sees in depth. Keep in mind that this is screen-space logic, so view dependence is part of the look.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Query distance field proximity to nearby surfaces.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: This is a high-value node for environment-aware effects, but it depends on distance field availability and project settings. Use it when contact behavior with nearby surfaces is the hero requirement.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Read the approximate scale of the object for scale-aware effects.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Use ObjectRadius when the effect should keep a similar visual ratio across differently sized meshes.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Anchor effects in world space around an object location.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Use object-position data when the effect must be stable in world space and tied to object location rather than only UV layout.

common_mistakes: using DepthFade as the main silhouette instead of as a final softening pass
forgetting that SceneDepth and PixelDepth are view-dependent and can change look with camera angle
using DistanceToNearestSurface without verifying distance fields are enabled and meaningful for the target assets
building object-scale-sensitive logic without ObjectRadius and then wondering why the effect breaks across mesh sizes

categories.display_name: Node UV nang cao va flipbook
categories.why_it_matters: These nodes and patterns give senior artists tighter control over radial motion, atlas playback, mesh-relative UV logic, and custom sheet sampling behavior.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Drive atlas frame playback, either through the built-in path or through custom math.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Use built-in ParticleSubUV or Flipbook logic first. Reach for custom Floor plus Frac logic when you need manual frame control, custom blending behavior, or a cheaper specialized variant.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Build custom frame stepping and interpolation math.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Do not rebuild flipbook logic by habit. Use Floor and Frac only when the stock SubUV route is not flexible enough for the effect's playback needs.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Convert UVs into polar-style radial coordinates.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: If the motion or shape is circular, radial, or angular, VectorToRadialValue is often a better start than forcing the look through flat Cartesian UV panning.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Generate normalized object-space coordinates based on mesh bounds.
typical_vfx_usage: consistent object-space gradients across scaled meshes
coverage masks independent of UV unwrap quality
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Use bounding-box UVW when the effect should follow the mesh volume or height consistently even if the UVs are poor or stretched.

common_mistakes: rebuilding custom flipbook math when ParticleSubUV already solves the problem cleanly
using radial logic on a shape that should read as directional flow instead of circular motion
forgetting that bounding-box-based coordinates depend on object bounds and can change if mesh scale changes in unexpected ways

categories.display_name: Node logic va toi uu hoa
categories.why_it_matters: Production VFX materials are often feature-rich master materials. These nodes control cost, variant support, and packed data usage without multiplying the runtime burden unnecessarily.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Compile shader variants that enable or disable features per material instance.
typical_vfx_usage: switch between cheap and hero variant
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Use Static Switch Parameter for feature families that should truly disappear from shader cost when disabled. Avoid turning every tiny artistic tweak into its own switch.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Branch shader behavior based on target platform capability.
typical_vfx_usage: reduced noise layers on weaker platforms
disable expensive distortion on low feature levels
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Use Feature Level Switch when the project supports multiple hardware tiers and the material needs clear high-end versus fallback behavior.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Extract selected channels from packed texture or data sources.
typical_vfx_usage: read emissive mask from one channel and erosion mask from another
separate RG motion vectors from A alpha
reduce texture sample count through channel packing
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: If the material relies on packed textures, ComponentMask is a first-class workflow tool, not just a convenience node. Document channel meaning clearly so packed maps remain maintainable.

common_mistakes: using too many Static Switch Parameters and creating an unmanageable master material explosion
forgetting to provide a clear cheap fallback path for heavy materials
packing many meanings into a texture without documenting channel ownership
using runtime math to emulate what a static compile-time switch should handle

categories.display_name: Node math va thu thuat procedural
categories.why_it_matters: These nodes and methods let senior artists create shapes, masks, and custom behavior without depending on external textures for every pattern.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Write custom shader logic directly when the standard graph becomes too limited or too heavy.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Use a Custom node only after a readable graph solution is understood. Custom HLSL is powerful, but it raises maintenance cost and should solve a real instruction, clarity, or capability problem.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Build procedural shapes and distance-driven masks without texture samples.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Distance is a core primitive for signed-distance-style logic. Combine it with subtract, abs, power, step, ceil, or smooth thresholds to get clean procedural forms.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Push alpha or mask contrast quickly and cheaply.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Prefer CheapContrast when the goal is simply to tighten a mask. Reach for Power only when the response curve specifically needs the power-function look.

common_mistakes: jumping to Custom HLSL before proving the graph logic and artistic goal
building a procedural shape system with no clear artistic controls exposed afterward
using high-complexity procedural logic where a single packed texture would be cheaper and easier to art direct
stacking contrast operations until the mask loses gradation and becomes brittle

categories.display_name: Node mesh data va vertex animation
categories.why_it_matters: These nodes matter when the effect depends on mesh topology, skinning state, VAT workflows, or deformation that must stay stable on animated characters and meshes.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Output deformed vertex positions at the material stage.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: World Position Offset is the main output gate for mesh deformation. Use it when actual silhouette or surface position change is required, not just color animation.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Provide the world-space normal direction used for outward displacement.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Pair Vertex Normal WS with World Position Offset when the deformation should move outward from the surface in a stable and readable way.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Read vertex position before skeletal skinning deformation.
typical_vfx_usage: material effects that should not swim on animated characters
VAT or deformation mappings on animated bodies
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Use Pre-Skinned Local Position when a character effect must stay locked to the body consistently before animation transforms distort the mapping.

common_mistakes: using animated world position data when the effect really needs stable pre-skin space
driving large WPO deformation without checking bounds, clipping, and readability
assuming VAT-like behavior can be improvised without stable coordinate conventions

if_you_need.need: camera-view-dependent depth comparison or underwater depth response
effect reacting to nearest environment surface
manual flipbook frame control or smooth custom atlas stepping
radial shockwave, magic circle, or portal motion
object-space gradient independent of UV unwrap quality
turn master-material features on or off cheaply per instance
procedural ring, circle, box, or custom shape math
stable mapping on a skinned character before animation distorts it

cross_reference_playbook.basic_prerequisite: Pair with Knowledge/Materials/Techniques/vfx_artist_essential_node_taxonomy.json for the foundational node layer.
cross_reference_playbook.material_math: Pair with Knowledge/Materials/Techniques/vfx_artist_material_math_taxonomy.json when the graph problem is primarily arithmetic, thresholds, trig, vector math, or packed-channel manipulation.
cross_reference_playbook.fire_and_smoke_flipbooks: Pair with Knowledge/Materials/Techniques/particle_subuv_flipbook_fire_smoke.json when the advanced logic is being applied to sprite-sheet fire or smoke materials.
cross_reference_playbook.radial_effects: Pair with Knowledge/Materials/Techniques/portal_ring.json when VectorToRadialValue and depth-aware ring shaping are central to the effect.
cross_reference_playbook.uv_motion_materials: Pair with Knowledge/Materials/Techniques/panning_uv.json when custom UV motion and advanced flow are part of the solution.
cross_reference_playbook.fresnel_shells: Pair with Knowledge/Materials/Techniques/fresnel.json when edge emphasis, shell glow, or view-dependent reads are still core to the look.

agent_guardrails: Start from the simplest readable graph first, then add advanced space, optimization, or procedural logic only when the effect goal truly needs it.
Depth-aware nodes are usually support logic for integration and polish, not the hero silhouette by themselves.
Prefer documented, reusable channel conventions and switch usage over one-off ad hoc graph logic.
If a custom HLSL node appears necessary, first write down what capability or instruction reduction it is replacing.
For skinned character effects, decide explicitly whether the mapping should live in world space, object space, or pre-skinned local space before building the graph.
